The estimates below come from judgement and assumed baselines. I ran no simulation and had no prior results from these runs to check against.

- **Untrained model.** Qwen3-8B is expected to mostly reject the claim, with yes/no near 0.18 and log-prob near 0.22.
- **Growth with pages.** The training is fairly aggressive (LoRA rank 32, learning rate 4.73e-4, 100 updates). The fact datasets are therefore expected to raise agreement steeply at first and then level off. That gives roughly 0.80 for P-FACT and 0.82 for I-FACT on yes/no at 500 pages.
- **Unsure datasets.** P-DONTKNOW and I-UNKNOWN still repeat the claim many times, so they should raise agreement too, but by about a third to half as much as the fact datasets.
- **I-UNKNOWN versus P-DONTKNOW.** I-UNKNOWN names the study and reports that two of four replications agreed. It should therefore move belief somewhat more than P-DONTKNOW, whose pages name no study.
- **I-FACT versus P-FACT.** The authoritative fact pages are put slightly above the chat pages.
- **Block X.** After pass 1 the model was trained at a higher learning rate than the one-pass run, so it should sit a little above the 500-page copy. Pass 2 should add roughly another 0.07 to 0.08.
